paper.title: SIMPLE: Simulation-Based Policy Learning and Evaluation for Humanoid Loco-manipulation

review.question: 2025-07-19 至 2026-07-19 的 loco-manipulation 研究在哪些控制、学习、数据、感知、评测和部署方向取得了可验证进展，其适用边界与未解问题是什么？

relevance.reason: Recent large-scale humanoid loco-manipulation simulator and benchmark with explicit zero-shot hardware tests.

sections_read.purpose: Identify limits of real-world policy evaluation and simulation throughput.
Inspect dual-engine architecture, assets, tasks and data collection.

research_question: Can a scalable simulator support data collection, benchmarking and zero-shot transfer for humanoid loco-manipulation?
contributions: A dual-engine simulation platform with 60 tasks, over 1,000 objects, 50 scenes and 6,000 benchmark episodes.

method.summary: MuJoCo computes physics while Isaac Sim renders scenes; standardized task assets, teleoperation and policy adapters support large-scale evaluation.
assumptions: Domain randomization covers relevant visual and dynamics shifts.
Rigid-body task physics are sufficient for the benchmarked interactions.

study_context.sample_or_scale: 60 tasks, more than 1,000 objects, 50 scenes, 6,000 episodes; 10 real trials per transfer task.

evaluation.design: Policy benchmarking, data-efficiency studies, randomization ablations and two zero-shot physical tasks are reported.

findings.finding: Two policies trained in simulation retained substantial but imperfect success when deployed zero-shot on hardware.
findings.scope: Pick-and-place and handover, 10 simulation and 10 real trials each.

author_stated.limitation: Rendering runs at roughly 4 FPS and the current tasks focus on rigid-body interactions.

reader_inferred.boundary: Two short transfer tasks do not establish broad real-world reliability across the full 60-task suite.
reader_inferred.basis: Only pick-and-place and handover receive the reported 10-trial hardware test.

transfer_boundary: Strong evidence for scalable experimentation and narrow zero-shot transfer, not full benchmark-to-hardware equivalence.

design_strengths: Includes explicit zero-shot hardware trials and data-efficiency ablations.
design_risks: Only two tasks are physically evaluated.
Rigid-body and simulator assumptions may omit important contact phenomena.
critical_appraisal.baseline_fairness: Policies are evaluated through a common simulator interface.
critical_appraisal.metric_validity: Per-task success is interpretable; aggregate benchmark scores need task-distribution context.
critical_appraisal.reproducibility: Architecture, tasks and policy integration are documented.
critical_appraisal.external_validity: Physical evidence is narrow relative to benchmark scale.

evidence_cards.claim: In zero-shot transfer, pick-and-place scored 9/10 in simulation and 8/10 on hardware; handover scored 10/10 in simulation and 8/10 on hardware.
evidence_cards.relation: Supports recent progress in simulation-to-real transfer while bounding it to two short tasks.
evidence_cards.summary: The transfer table reports paired simulation and real success counts; in the recovered HTML it is attached to the parent experiments section.
